public_rationale: Evidence available by mid-2026 shows AI's measured productivity effect was small. An NBER-summarized survey of nearly 6,000 executives (Nov 2025–Jan 2026) found 89% reported no impact on labor productivity. Among firms that did report effects, the average boost was 0.29%. The Penn Wharton Budget Model estimated AI added just 0.01 points to productivity growth in 2025. Meanwhile, prominent forecasts such as Goldman Sachs's had predicted large gains, and executives themselves expected much bigger effects ahead. A smaller impact so far than many expected is consistent with this record.
limitations: Many forecasts covered a decade, so a small effect so far does not prove them wrong.
Strong macro productivity readings in 2025 leave room for debate about AI's role.
The survey data are self-reported by executives.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: measured productivity gains from AI up to mid-2026 have been small, while widely publicized expectations pointed to large gains.
Evidence on measured impact (firm surveys, macro estimates) up to the post date is outcome evidence. Earlier published forecasts show what was anticipated.
criteria.support_condition: Credible studies up to June 2026 find small measured productivity effects from AI, alongside prominent expectations of much larger effects.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible studies up to June 2026 attribute large, clearly measured productivity gains to AI that match or exceed prominent expectations.

evidence.excerpt: More than 90 percent of executives report no effect of AI use on employment over the past three years, and 89 percent report no impact on labor productivity. Among the minority that do report effects, the results tilt slightly positive for productivity, with an estimated average boost of 0.29 percent.
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER Digest)
evidence.explanation: A survey of nearly 6,000 executives (Nov 2025–Jan 2026) found that most firms saw no productivity effect from AI. That points to a small real-world impact so far.

evidence.excerpt: we estimate that AI’s impact on TFP growth remains small today - 0.01 percentage points (pp) in 2025 - as most businesses have yet to deploy and gain experience with AI tools.
evidence.locator: Section 'Generative AI’s Projected Impact on TFP', paragraph 1
evidence.explanation: Penn Wharton estimates AI added almost nothing to economy-wide productivity growth in 2025.
